$comment: Realisation in uz (docs/rules/uz.md; ADR 0158): uz merges lexemes, so a cell is realised through the lexemes that bring it (a finite verb's VerbForm=Fin and person, a nominal's case, the zeros nom, p3 and imp.sg among them) and a token as the course lists its lexemes, with `spellings: false`; the steps are the rewrites that ran (vowel drop, voicing), never a merge. One vector or more per affix and allomorph condition, each a form the course writes but where a note says otherwise (a lexeme of the lexicon, or one given with uz's affixes, where no word of the course has it); then tokens as the course lists their lexemes.

vectors.note: Bilmayman (bil + neg + pres + cop-1sg): the course writes it, and gives it bilmoq as its lemma.
The course's ichadi: -a after a consonant, then -di.
The course's ishlayman: -y after a vowel.
The course's iching: -ing after a consonant.
The course's yeng: -ng after a vowel.
Kechirasiz, the lemma the course gives kechirmoq.
Toʻydim, the lemma the course gives toymoq.
The course's Akalarim: -lar, then -im after its consonant.
The course's onam: -m after a vowel.
uygacha: no noun of the course is written with -gacha (beshgacha is a number's).
Kuzda, the lemma the course gives kuz.
Oʻngga, the lemma the course gives ong.
Doʻstim, the lemma the course gives dost.
Boshqasi, the lemma the course gives boshqa.
singillarim: the vowel of -lar does not drop.
Blocking off passes the class over: singilim, the form a learner may build.
Singil's third person, a listed stem (Hancock-Parmer p. 63: singlisi).
mushugi: a noun of the lexicon (the course writes mushuk alone).

notes.en: Qayerdansiz? Where are you from? Ishdan: from work.
Choyingizni iching: drink your tea. An object that is not definite takes nothing: choy iching.
Arzonroq: cheaper. Arzonroq qiling! Make it cheaper!

gloss.en: -siz: you are (polite; suffix on the predicate)

notes.en: Ikkita kitob: two books. Nechta? How many? Numbers work with or without it.
-ka after k (parkka), -qa after q (qishloqqa). Men + -ga = menga: to me.
men + -ning is written mening.
-ing after a consonant (iching, oling), -ng after a vowel (yeng).

gloss.en: the imperative to one person you know well: the stem alone (ich! "drink!")
-moq: the infinitive, how a verb is cited (ichmoq "to drink")

notes.en: Uyda: at home. Toshkentda: in Tashkent. Men uydaman: I am at home.
Ye + -ma + -y + -man = yemayman: I don't eat.

gloss.en: the nominative: no ending (the subject; an object that is not definite)
he, she, it: no ending (the past: keldi "came"; edi "was")

notes.en: Keldi: he/she came. With a person ending: keldim, keldingiz, keldik.
Keldik: we came.
Keldim: I came.
Keldingiz: you came.
Not used after numbers: ikki kitob, two books.
-imiz after a consonant (uyimiz), -miz after a vowel (oilamiz).
-i after a consonant (ismi), -si after a vowel (onasi).
-a after a consonant (ichaman), -y after a vowel (yeyman, ishlayman), then a person ending: -man I, -siz you, -di he/she, -miz we.
Ichadi: he/she drinks. After -yap it is -ti: uxlayapti.
Nima qilyapsiz? What are you doing? Kitob oʻqiyapman: I am reading. He/she: -yapti.

gloss.en: -gacha: until, up to, as far as

notes.en: Toʻqqizdan beshgacha: from nine to five.
Olmoqchiman: I want to buy. Bormoqchimiz: we want to go, we plan to go.

parki: a noun of one syllable keeps its k.
mushukka: only before the possessive's i.

vectors.note: qishloqqa: -qa after q (Hancock-Parmer p. 59), a noun the lexicon does not hold.
parkkacha: -kacha after k, as the dative.
The course's nechta: necha's nech before -ta.
The course's edim: the stem e- before its ending.
The course's ich: the stem alone.
The course's uydaman: an ending no rule of the noun writes, as the token lists it.
Hammasi, the lemma the course gives hamma: pinned (no rule for pronouns).
